messages:
jess_support: Customer reports intermittent 502 / TLS handshake failures to our Hosted API after they switched traffic to their VPC endpoint (VPCE). Errors only come from two subnets, other subnets in same VPC are fine. They see 'TLS record type 22' then connection reset in their client logs. They say they allowed outbound to our NLB IPs and added privatelink to allowlist. :worried:
sam_eng: Can you paste the VPCE id and the route table entries for the subnets that fail? Also need SGs and NACLs attached. Are they using NLB or ALB behind the VPCE?
jess_support: VPCE: vpce-0a1b2c3d4e, failing subnets route table -> 10.0.1.0/24 -> local, no explicit route to vpce. SG on ENI allows outbound 443 to 0.0.0.0/0. NACLs default. They said PrivateLink was created pointing to our NLB.
maria_sre: If route table has only local and no explicit proxy route that's fine for interface endpoints, but check SNAT on their NAT/Egress. Does their egress path rewrite source IPs? Also verify source/destination check on the endpoint ENIs (should be enabled).
sam_eng: Two common gotchas: 1) Firewall/NGW that does TLS intercept (breaks SNI) 2) NLB configured with proxy protocol or TLS termination mismatch. Ask them to run: curl -v --resolve api.redwood:443:<vpce-eni-ip> https://api.redwood/ and paste output. Also tcpdump on the ENI for SYN/SYN-ACK/FIN.
jess_support: Pasted customer's curl output (sanitized):
-----
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood/
* Connected to 10.2.3.45 (10.2.3.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate (11)
* SSL certificate problem: certificate is not yet valid
-----
They also included this tcpdump snippet:
10:12:34.123456 IP 10.2.3.12.51234 > 10.2.3.45.443: Flags [S], seq 0
10:12:34.123457 IP 10.2.3.45.443 > 10.2.3.12.51234: Flags [R], seq 0
-----
maria_sre: Certificate not yet valid could mean time skew on the NLB target or the service side. But RST back from 10.2.3.45 suggests something actively refusing connection (NACL or host-level firewall). Ask them to check instance/target health on our side for that VPCE target IP. I can query NLB health if you give me the VPCE mapping.
sam_eng: Also ask them whether they have a proxy/inspection device doing TLS rewrap — that often returns a cert that doesn't match time or CN and then client aborts. If only two subnets fail, maybe those subnets egress through an inline proxy.
jess_support: Customer confirmed: failing subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 -> TransitGW -> Firewall cluster (TLS inspect). Working subnets go direct to IGW. They added our NLB IPs to allowlist but the firewall is still intercepting.
maria_sre: Ok that explains the cert mismatch + RSTs. Two action items: 1) Have them bypass TLS inspect for traffic to our service (match by SNI or destination ENI IPs) OR 2) terminate TLS at the firewall and ensure it reissues certs trusted by their clients and preserves SNI. Prefer (1).
sam_eng: Also confirmed we recently rolled a change to the VPCE routing policies? deploy-bot: "vpce-config-bump: route-policy-update applied by infra at 2024-09-10T09:58:12Z" :information_source:
jess_support: I've asked the customer to open a bypass rule for SNI api.redwood or for destination IPs 10.2.3.45/32 and to run the curl + tcpdump again.
maria_sre: If they can't bypass, ask them to capture server-side SNI in our logs and we'll verify what SNI the client sends (could be stripped). Also check TLS versions/ALPN — some TLS-inspectors don't support TLS1.3 and will force TLS1.2 which can cause unexpected behavior with certain NLB configs.
sam_eng: Last check: confirm that the VPCE is interface endpoint type and not gateway, and that it's associated with the correct security group allowing inbound health checks from our NLB. If health checks fail our targets may drop connections.
jess_support: Customer replied: will try bypass rule and come back with updated tcpdump. :thumbsup:
maria_sre: Great, add suggested repro steps for them: 1) curl -v --tlsv1.2 -H "Host: api.redwood" https://<vpce-eni-ip>/ 2) tcpdump -ni eth0 host <client-ip> and host <vpce-eni-ip> 3) share NACL/RTB screenshots and firewall policy for that traffic. Keep me tagged and I'll check backend metrics.
sam_eng: I'll also check target health and cert validity on our NLB for the endpoint IPs. If we see time skew we'll escalate to infra.
jess_support: Customer will escalate to their firewall team, ETA 2 hours. Leaving thread open.
